column1:
Incorporating Beige Book insights alongside the FOMC’s December 16, 2020 statement slightly deepens the cautious tone. While policy remains highly accommodative (near-zero rates and ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases supporting market functioning), District reports point to modest-to-moderate growth that was slowing amid renewed COVID-19 waves. Contacts noted ongoing pandemic-related disruptions to producers and shippers (reinforcing operational frictions), uneven labor market healing with particular weakness in services (e.g., leisure/hospitality), and persistent softness in commercial real estate. On credit, bank-intermediated channels remained restrictive: loan demand was mixed to weak and standards tighter, echoing SLOOS; however, housing stayed a relative bright spot with strong activity in safer, GSE-eligible mortgage segments. Overall, the Beige Book corroborates downside risks to activity and employment in the near term, with some offsets from housing and continued policy support. Net effect: a modestly more negative tilt than the initial read.
